Context Rot: How Increasing Input Tokens Impacts LLM Performance | Chroma

Finished all my paper presentations at ASE 2026! 🎉 With the increasingly widespread use of large language models (LLMs) and coding agents, the verifiability, reliability, and security of software systems are becoming issues of significant concern within both the academia and industry. This research topic sits precisely at the intersection of software engineering, artificial intelligence, and systems—an area that also aligns perfectly with our lab's research focus. At Middleware Systems Research Group (MSRG) lab (lead by Prof. Arno Jacobsen), we began by studying microservice root cause analysis, and are now actively expanding our research scope to related areas such as program repair and agentic system analysis.

Thank you all to the wonderful discussions happened during the talk and after: Minghua Ma, Ryan Zhang, Joost Noppen, Federica Sarro, Chunyang Chen, Matthias Schlaipfer, Golnaz Gharachorlu, PhD, Haitam EL Hayani and many more. Best of luck with your research and hope to see you again soon in other conferences!

The presented papers are available on ACM now:
1. GALA: Graph-Augmented LLM Agents for Root Cause Analysis and Incident Response in Microservices
https://lnkd.in/e8jz23BG

2. AgentChaosBench: Benchmarking External Fault Detection and Localization in Agentic Systems
https://lnkd.in/enNz9P23

3. When Log Parsing Removes What Matters: Detecting Failures in Distributed GPU Workloads (Boyuan Cui good job on presenting this one!)
https://lnkd.in/e9XtdH_s

Well deserved, Jackson and the #SREGym team! AI for SRE is in an unusual situation, where no strong benchmark is available and the technical landscape is rather opaque. The fundamental challenge is to curate high-quality problems that can reflect real-world characteristics of SRE tasks. It's great to see #SREGym continuously pushing on this grand challenge, meanwhile offering an open platform for everyone, and more importantly, the active community they have built. The #SREGym Slack has 250+ members and the project has 60+ contributors. The best part is to hear from more and more practitioners who are using it and giving invaluable feedback.

See Jackson's post: https://lnkd.in/p/gwYxyHHd for more information (LinkedIn should not discourage repost).
